title: bhps chief commercial officer step down january internal memo shows 2026 09 02
text:
MELBOURNE, Sept 2 (Reuters) - BHP's Chief Commercial Officer Rag ​Udd will step down at the end of January ‌to pursue an opportunity outside the company, according to a staff memo seen by Reuters on Tuesday, leaving open one of the miner's most ​difficult roles — negotiating iron ore deals with China.
He had been ​seen by some analysts and investors as a contender ⁠for the top job at BHP (BHP.AX)
, opens new tab
, . That position went to ​Brandon Craig who started in July.
Udd did not immediately respond to ​a Reuters request for comment.
Udd, who is based in Singapore, will have worked at BHP for three decades by the time of his departure, according ​to the memo.
He was in charge of BHP's negotiations with China ​Mineral Resources Group (CMRG) at a time when the state buyer ramped up pressure ‌on ⁠BHP and other iron ore miners to win better terms for its steel makers.
That pressure resulted in a number of bans on steel mills from buying its products late last year until ​a deal was struck in ​April.
Iron ore makers ⁠expect those negotiations to get harder, and selecting the best leader to manage that key relationship ​will be a top priority for Craig.
Previously, Udd ​led BHP's ⁠Americas division from 2020 to 2024, overseeing the development of the Jansen potash project in Canada that is set to start production ⁠mid ​next year.
He also oversaw major investments across ​BHP's Chilean copper operations including the Spence expansion and Escondida, the world's largest copper ​mine.
